Freedom and Responsibility

1. Every year on Independence Day, schools across India ring with songs about freedom. Yet freedom is not only a gift won by those who struggled before us; it is also a responsibility that each generation must carry.

2. A free citizen has the right to speak, to vote, to travel and to choose a profession. But these rights come with duties. The right to speak carries the duty not to spread lies. The right to vote carries the duty to vote thoughtfully. The right to use public spaces carries the duty to keep them clean.

3. History shows that freedom can be lost not only to foreign rulers but also to carelessness. When citizens stop caring about public life, leaving every decision to a few, democracy weakens from within.

4. Young people have a special role. They are often the first to question injustice and the most eager to change things. When their energy is joined to knowledge and patience, they can strengthen the freedom they have inherited.

5. The writer concludes that freedom is like a garden. It was planted by others, but it will bloom only if each generation waters it.

(ii) Give a suitable title for the passage other than the one given.
(iii) What duty comes with the right to speak?

(viii) Why do young people have a special role?  (a) They have more time to vote  (b) They question injustice first and are eager to change things  (c) They are always right  (d) They are rich
(ix) What must young people's energy be joined to?
(x) Explain the comparison of freedom to a garden.

(vii) (b) weakens (viii) (b) They question injustice first and are eager to change things (ix) Knowledge and patience. 1. In every Indian city there are people who help strangers without ever being thanked. A tea-seller near a hospital keeps a free kettle for the relatives of patients. 3. Small acts can have large effects. A study of volunteers found that people who helped others regularly reported better health and less stress. Giving, it seems, is good not only for the receiver but also for the giver.

4. Schools can play a part. When students are encouraged to help a classmate, visit an old-age home or collect books for a village library, they learn that kindness is a habit, not an accident.

Freedom and Responsibility

1. Every year on Independence Day, schools across India ring with songs about freedom. Yet freedom is not only a gift won by those who struggled before us; it is also a responsibility that each generation must carry.

2. A free citizen has the right to speak, to vote, to travel and to choose a profession. But these rights come with duties. The right to speak carries the duty not to spread lies. The right to vote carries the duty to vote thoughtfully. The right to use public spaces carries the duty to keep them clean.

3. History shows that freedom can be lost not only to foreign rulers but also to carelessness. When citizens stop caring about public life, leaving every decision to a few, democracy weakens from within.

4. Young people have a special role. They are often the first to question injustice and the most eager to change things. When their energy is joined to knowledge and patience, they can strengthen the freedom they have inherited.
